title: Potato Salad with Egg, Made with Italian Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: A salad of boiled potatoes, hard‑boiled eggs and vegetables, tossed with an Italian dressing (olive oil, vinegar, mustard, herbs). It is a light dish popular in summer and at picnics.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Italian dressing gives the salad a distinctive aroma of basil, oregano and garlic.
In warm weather many Russians replace the traditional “Olivier” with this lighter potato‑egg salad.
Eggs add an extra source of protein, making the dish more filling.
Potatoes retain a good amount of vitamin C when not overcooked.
The salad can be prepared ahead, but add the dressing just before serving to avoid soggy potatoes.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and potatoes provide vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Olive oil in the Italian dressing is high in monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Potato skins and added vegetables (e.g., green onions) contribute fiber for better digestion.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates (potato) and protein (egg) helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Herbs such as basil and oregano contain polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: If salt is added to the dressing, the dish can become too salty, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Eggs must be fully cooked and the finished salad stored in the refrigerator for no more than 2‑3 days.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Olive oil increases the calorie count; portion control is advised for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a side dish or a light main course. It can be eaten with a fork or spoon, or used as a filling for sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Stir before serving to redistribute the dressing. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
